title: Unified Inference: V2 Product PRD, Roadmap, Pricing & Release Notes
author: Avery Chen
body:
Summary:
This document consolidates the product definition, high-level design, roadmap, pricing & packaging, and initial release notes for Unified Inference V2 (UI-V2). UI-V2 is the next major step in Redwood's product surface to: unify serving semantics across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments; provide stronger cost controls and auto-optimizations (Redwood Optimize integration); and introduce a single rollout/control plane for model variants and fallback policies.

Audience:
- Product management, engineering, platform, sales enablement, and SRE.

1) Product overview
===================
Goal:
- Provide a single API and control plane that guarantees predictable latency and cost across deployment modes while enabling automated quality-preserving optimizations.
Key outcomes:
- Unified API and model catalog across Hosted / Dedicated / Private.
- Smart routing with policy-driven fallbacks and region-aware capacity selection.
- Integrated Redwood Optimize suggestions (batching, quantization profiles, caching).
- Observability: per-route token cost, latency heatmaps, and quality regression alerts.
Primary users:
- ML engineers integrating models into product flows, platform teams standardizing inference, and product engineers building chat/generation features.

2) Product goals and success metrics
===================================
Primary goals (12-month horizon):
- Reduce average per-token serving cost by 20% for customers who adopt the recommended Optimize suggestions.
- Maintain 99.9% availability for Dedicated customers and 99.5% for Hosted API (measured monthly).
- Decrease median 90th-percentile tail latency for short-text generation (<=256 tokens) by 25% compared to V1.
- Achieve 30% of new enterprise opportunities to choose Dedicated or Private within 6 months of pilots.
Metrics (tracked in Console dashboards):
- Per-route cost/unit (USD per 1k tokens), latency p50/p90/p99, error rate, model-quality regression rate (per evaluation suite), adoption rate for Optimize suggestions.

3) Scope and non-goals
======================
In scope for V2:
- API parity for text generation, chat (structured messages), embeddings, and reranking.
- Model variant rollouts (canary / A/B) and automatic fallback to quantized variants.
- Redwood Optimize integration (read-only suggestions for V2 GA; auto-apply in a later patch).
- Console UX for per-route cost and rollout controls.
Out of scope for V2:
- Full auto-apply of Optimize profiles across private on-prem installs (pilot-only).
- Native model training services.

4) Requirements (functional & non-functional)
============================================
High-level functional requirements (table):
| id | requirement | acceptance criteria | owner | priority |
|-----|--------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------|----------|
| FR-1 | Unified endpoint semantics across deployments | Same API surface and consistent response schema for Hosted/Dedicated/Private for text, chat, embeddings, rerank. Automated test coverage (>=90%). | Product / API | P0 |
| FR-2 | Model variant rollouts and policy-driven fallback | Canary and A/B support, policy config UI, health checks and automatic fallback to compatible variant within 5s on failure. | Eng-Serving-Runtime | P0 |
| FR-3 | Smart routing by latency/cost/region | Policy language and router implementation with SLA-aware decisions; documented routing precedence. | Eng-Platform | P1 |
| FR-4 | Optimize suggestions surfaced in Console | Per-route suggestions for batching, quantization, and cache TTL with estimated savings and quality impact. | Redwood-Optimize / Product | P1 |
| NFR-1 | Latency SLOs | Hosted: 99.5% requests < 300ms for <=128 tokens; Dedicated: 99.9% < 250ms for <=128 tokens, measured p95. | Eng-SRE | P0 |
| NFR-2 | Security and compliance | Support KMS integration, audit logs, and RBAC for Private deployments. | Security | P0 |
| NFR-3 | Cost reporting | Token-level cost attribution in Console with daily and hourly rollups. | Finance + Eng-Platform | P0 |

Detailed technical requirements:
- API: OpenAPI-compatible schema; streaming support for generation; function/tool-calling metadata preserved.
- Model catalog: version pinning, compatibility metadata (quantized flag, compatible runtime), and performance profile (cost per token, latency percentiles).
- Router: pluggable decision engine; fallback latency budget default = 5s; policy precedence = [customer overrides, region affinity, cost tiers, latency SLO].
- Observability: traces correlated with request IDs, token-level cost granularity, and a QA evaluation harness to flag quality regressions tied to rollout changes.

5) Design specs (high-level)
===========================
Architecture overview:
- Control plane: manages model catalog, rollout configs, and Optimize suggestions. Stateless API frontends call runtime endpoints.
- Serving runtime: GPU-optimized processes with KV cache managers, continuous batching, and quantization-aware execution paths.
- Router: sits between API frontends and runtime; evaluates routing policies, enforces fallbacks, and records decisions to tracing.

Key design decisions:
- Variant compatibility model: variants must register compatibility matrix (max-sequence, supported ops, quantized flag). Router validates compatibility at decision time.
- Fallback semantics: failure modes include runtime error, overloaded GPU, and quality regression. Fallback sequence tries (in order) same-variant on other capacity, quantized-compatible variant, older stable variant, then static canned response if configured.
- Optimize suggestions: computed offline by Optimize service using workload traces and a cost/quality simulator; surfaced with estimated savings and an A/B quality delta.

API contract examples (excerpt):
- POST /v2/generate
  body: {"model": "redwood-unified-1", "input": "...", "max_tokens": 128, "timeout_ms": 2000, "rollout_id": "canary-2026-02"}
- Response includes metadata block: {"model_version":"1.2.3","variant":"aq-8bit-q2","cost_estimate_usd_per_1k_tokens":"0.19","trace_id":"..."}

6) UX / Console requirements
==========================
- Per-route dashboard: cost estimate, p50/p90 latency, error rate, Optimize suggestions (with one-click copy-to-CLI).
- Rollout page: configure canary %, health checks, automatic rollback threshold (default error rate delta > 0.5%).
- Billing integration: per-route cost attribution with export to CSV and daily webhook to finance.

7) Roadmap and milestones
========================
Quarterly roadmap (high level):
- Q4 2025 (completed): V1 unify API; early Optimize integration (read-only); Dedicated capacity improvements.
- Q1 2026 (GA target): UI-V2 GA for Hosted and Dedicated with unified API, model variant rollouts, routing policies, and Console surfacing for Optimize suggestions.
- Q2 2026: Private deployment support for UI-V2 (V1 compatibility mode), auto-apply Optimize in UI for Hosted, advanced routing rules (user-level overrides), early enterprise pilots for on-prem.
- Q3 2026: Auto-apply for Private (alpha), additional quantization profiles support, cross-region failover automation.

Milestones for Q1 2026 (detailed):
1. Feature freeze: 2026-01-15
2. Internal dogfood & enterprise pilot start: 2026-01-30
3. Beta (external) release: 2026-02-10
4. GA cut: 2026-02-28

8) Pricing & packaging notes
===========================
Objectives:
- Keep Hosted usage-based pricing with clear cost signals (per-token + per-request surcharge for short latency SLOs).
- Dedicated: reserved capacity with monthly/annual commits and optional burst credits.
- Private: platform license + per-GPU seat pricing and optional support tiers.
Pricing table (illustrative):
| offering | billing model | starter price (monthly) | notes |
|----------|---------------|------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Hosted Standard | usage (per token) | N/A | $0.060 / 1k tokens baseline for text gen; different tiers for embeddings & rerank. |
| Hosted Low-Latency | usage + SLO surcharge | +$0.015 / 1k tokens | For p95 <= 150ms targets; surcharge applied per-route. |
| Dedicated | committed monthly | from $25k / month | Commit for GPU pool; pricing varies by GPU type and reserved throughput. |
| Private | license + infra | from $100k / year + infra | Platform license + deployment/ops support; enterprise pricing for on-prem. |
Packaging notes:
- Offer an "Optimize Starter" add-on with 90-day consult + retention of advanced suggestions for $5k/month.
- Discounting guidance: 15-25% off listed price for annual commitments > $300k.
- Marketplace offers: enable Dedicated via cloud marketplace for quicker procurement.

9) Rollout plan and runbooks
===========================
High-level rollout strategy:
1. Internal dogfood on Redwood product flows and 2 internal enterprise customers.
2. Invite-based Beta with 5-10 external customers (focus on ML-platform & product teams).
3. GA with gradual ramp and usage-based throttles for initial 30 days.

Rollback & escalation runbook (summary):
1. If error rate delta > 0.5% over baseline for 10 minutes -> automatic rollback of rollout to previous stable variant.
2. If tail latency regressions exceed 20% for > 15m -> route traffic to Dedicated fallback pool and page the on-call (eng-sre).
3. Major quality regression detected by evaluation harness -> pause rollouts for all customers using that model and open incident.

10) Release notes (initial GA cut 2026-02-28)
==========================================
Version: UI-V2 GA (2026-02-28)
Highlights:
- Unified API for text, chat, embeddings, and reranking across Hosted and Dedicated.
- Model variant rollouts (canary/A-B) with automatic fallbacks.
- Smart routing policies (latency, cost, region, customer tier).
- Console: per-route cost breakdown, Optimize suggestions, rollout controls.
- Observability: token-level cost attribution, per-route latency heatmaps, and integrated QA evaluation alerts.
Known limitations / caveats:
- Optimize auto-apply is disabled for Private GA (read-only suggestions only).
- Some legacy Dedicated SKUs require a short conversion window; customers will be contacted with migration instructions.
- Private on-prem packaging requires additional validation steps and may be available under NDA for initial pilots.

11) Ownership & contacts
=======================
Product owner: Avery Chen (product)
Engineering leads: Samir Gupta (eng-serving-runtime), Priya Menon (eng-platform)
SRE lead: Marcus Patel
Security contact: Lena Ortiz
Sales enablement: Jordan Reyes

12) Open risks and mitigation
===========================
- Risk: Quality regressions from aggressive quantization.
  Mitigation: pre-flight evaluation harness, staged canaries, and default disable of auto-apply for critical routes.
- Risk: Customer confusion on new pricing tiers.
  Mitigation: clear pricing pages, migration playbook, and customer success outreach.
- Risk: Cross-region routing complexity and data residency.
  Mitigation: region-aware policy defaults and explicit residency flags for Private.

Appendices
==========
A. CLI examples
- Create rollout: redwood rollout create --route "/chat/gpt" --model redwood-unified-1 --canary 5 --health-check "latency<300ms"
- Query cost: redwood billing route-usage --route "/embedding/text" --start 2026-02-01 --end 2026-02-28

B. Acceptance test checklist (sample)
1. API parity tests pass (>=95% of canonical test cases).
2. Console shows per-route cost for test routes.
3. Canary rollback triggers within SLA on induced errors.
4. Optimize suggestions are visible and estimate savings > 5% for sample workloads.
